coverage.reason: States that Rule 6c-11 covers ETFs organized as registered open-end management investment companies. It also lists unit-investment-trust ETFs as needing separate exemptive relief.
States that leveraged and inverse ETFs 'can also rely on 6c-11; they are no longer categorically excluded' and 'must comply with applicable Rule 18f-4 requirements.'

Says nontransparent/semitransparent active ETFs and ETF share classes need separate exemptive relief. It also notes the daily portfolio transparency condition. Master-feeder structures are omitted, so the bundle is substantive but incomplete.

rationale: No central error: the answer does not exclude leveraged/inverse ETFs, does not treat UITs as covered, and does not claim nontransparent ETFs or share classes avoid separate relief. The ancillary statements on 18f-4 grandfathering and commodity pools are not materially false. Coverage is 2.5 of 3 because master-feeder is missing from point 3, so not every required minimum is met. The grade is therefore partial.
